analysis.title: GS US TMT .. stocks (CDNS, FOWNK, Memory, Semis) ..
key_insights: Futures bid (NDX Fut +55 bps) with crude and rates slightly lower ahead of a busy 3-day stretch of FOMC plus large-cap tech earnings. Korea and Japan rose 2-3% overnight on better earnings, while Europe traded lower (France -24 bps) as regional consumer confidence hit 13-year lows.

Semis: SOX tested its 200-day moving average last week for the first time since June 2025. The desk says positioning is cleaner but sentiment is not outright bearish, fundamentals are strong (capex and EPS estimates still rising) and SOX trades at about a 1x discount to its 15-year average valuation.

Semis: investors are hesitant to step back into the capex and supply chain trade until the market rewards companies for estimate revisions rather than compressing multiples on 'peak' concerns (LRCX and WDC last week). SOX rose 280 bps yesterday, its best day since late September.

CDNS: debate is whether EDA names can move from AI overhang (e.g. open-source AI disruption) to clearer AI beneficiaries, which the desk calls one of the more powerful multiple-enhancing events (Security Software is the clearest example). Cadence delivered solid earnings and GIR believes strong guidance suggests AI tool adoption and recurring revenue growth are taking hold.

Memory: Hynix, Samsung, STX and SNDK all report this week. The debate is how to reconcile strong DRAM prices and supply/demand with transitions that cap returns and compress multiples. A TrendForce webinar saw positive DRAM pricing through 2027 and into 1H28, with meaningful DRAM capacity additions unlikely before 2028 despite aggressive capex plans.

FWONK (Formula One): forward EV/EBITDA is at all-time lows despite a known tactical bear case. GIR estimates canceled 4Q events could cost up to ~$40M, or ~3% of FY2026 consolidated Adjusted OIBDA estimates, and sees an attractive 2027 set-up from easing comps and sponsorship and licensing execution. TKO is also making new 52-week lows.

Top client inbounds yesterday: whether the semis bounce is real, NFLX weakness, broader Internet weakness (RDDT, EBAY), earnings set-ups (AMZN, MSFT, SNDK, NOW), no bounce yet in SE, and whether the TXN move is durable.

Earnings one-liners: RCL delivered the second solid cruise print in a month with yields accelerating into 4Q/2027. Hilton reported +7% US RevPAR in 3Q but the stock fell on debate over 3Q flow-through and the 4Q guide. JCI rose 5% as Q4 organic orders accelerated 44% with backlog of $23bn, up 43% y/y. Mercedes fell 4% on a warning citing China headwinds and 4Q costs.
Events today: CLS Investor Day 8am ET, GWRE Investor Day 1:30pm ET, INTU Connect and ORCL AIWorld conferences. Earnings tonight: CSGP, FFIV, HOOD, LOGI, NXPI, ST, STX, TER, Visa.
